context:
Follow the ClickHouse query transformer pattern exactly:
- Reference: benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/query_transformer.py (class structure, transform() entry point, transformations_applied tracking)
- Reference: benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/workload.py:293-295 (integration into execute_query())
- Reference: benchbox/core/tpch/dataframe_queries.py (DataFrame implementations of Q11, Q16, Q18, Q20 show the correct algorithmic approach to translate into SQL rewrites)

Use query_id-based dispatch rather than regex pattern matching on SQL text.
Each rewrite method extracts parameterized values (nation names, thresholds,
dates) from the qgen SQL via targeted regex, then reconstructs the query with
DataFusion-compatible structure. Literal values are preserved; only structure changes.
description:
DataFusion's SQL engine misexecutes 4 TPC-H queries (Q11, Q16, Q18, Q20) that
use SQL patterns it handles differently from PostgreSQL: HAVING with scalar
subqueries, NOT IN subqueries, IN with HAVING, and nested correlated subqueries.

These failures were exposed when the seed parity fix changed validation from
"loose" (±50% tolerance) to "exact" (0% tolerance). The DataFrame implementations
of the same queries produce correct results because they use explicit joins,
anti-joins, and semi-joins instead of these problematic SQL patterns.

The fix follows the established ClickHouse pattern: create a DataFusionQueryTransformer
that rewrites the 4 problematic queries before execution, transforming them into
semantically equivalent SQL that DataFusion handles correctly.

Row count discrepancies at SF=1 with qgen -d defaults:
  Q11: Expected 1,048 → Got 1,289 (HAVING + scalar subquery threshold)
  Q16: Expected 18,314 → Got 18,200 (NOT IN subquery, NULL semantics)
  Q18: Expected 57 → Got 9 (IN subquery with HAVING clause)
  Q20: Expected 186 → Got 173 (nested IN with correlated subquery)

anti_patterns.dont: add rewrites to the SQLGlot translation layer
anti_patterns.instead: keep rewrites in the platform adapter
anti_patterns.why: the issue is DataFusion execution semantics not SQL syntax

anti_patterns.dont: modify qgen output or query templates
anti_patterns.instead: rewrite at the adapter level instead
anti_patterns.why: they are the official TPC-H reference
it is independent and already working

anti_patterns.dont: use generic regex-based SQL rewriting for complex structural changes
anti_patterns.instead: use query_id dispatch with targeted extraction instead
anti_patterns.why: nested SQL regex is fragile and unmaintainable

preserves.behavior: All 18 non-affected TPC-H queries (Q1-Q10, Q12-Q15, Q17, Q19, Q21-Q22) pass through transformer unchanged
DataFusion DataFrame mode (datafusion-df) execution path is not affected
DataFusionAdapter.execute_query() continues to work for non-TPC-H queries (no transformer applied when query_id is not Q11/Q16/Q18/Q20)

verifications.description: Existing DataFusion adapter tests still pass
